In a large Syrian–Lebanese X-linked thrombocytopenia family, affected men carried the missense C168T (Thr45Met) mutation in exon 2 of the WASp gene, which the authors describe as the most frequent missense mutation at exon 2, the commonest site for XLT and mild WAS mutations.

For the neighbouring L101P mutation (not Thr45Met), affected patients showed severe suppression of WASP protein levels, and molecular modeling proposed that P101 induces a conformational change in Q99 that breaks its hydrogen bond with WIP Y475.
No functional assay covers residue 45 of P42768 (functional_assays_covering_residue = 0).
payload.why_it_matters: Without an assay at this residue, the pathogenicity evidence at position 45 rests on clinical records and computational predictions, not on a measured functional effect.

payload.statement: EVH1 domains are about 115 residues long and adopt the pleckstrin homology fold; four protein families, including WASP, contain EVH1 domains that bind proline-rich sequences.
Of the 1 experimental structure observing residue 45 (PDB 9S9X), none has the residue mutated (of_those_with_the_residue_mutated = 0), so no experimental structure of T45M was reported.
payload.why_it_matters: Structural consequences of Met at position 45 cannot be read from experiment; only the reference residue is observed in the one structure.

payload.statement: Mutations in the WAS gene can produce distinct syndrome variants that largely, though not exclusively, depend on the mutation; premature termination and deletions abrogate WASp expression.
The structure ledger lists no ligands across all observing structures (distinct_ligands = 0, ligands_across_all_observing_structures empty).
payload.why_it_matters: No ligand contact is recorded at residue 45, so ligand-binding mechanisms cannot be supported or excluded from the starting evidence; the ligand contact test is the place to measure this.

payload.statement: No retrieved study measured WASp protein level, folding, or stability for the Thr45Met substitution itself.
payload.why_it_matters: Whether Thr45Met lowers WASp abundance or leaves a stable protein that is functionally impaired decides between expression-loss and intrinsic-function mechanisms, and the retrieved literature does not separate them.

payload.statement: The retrieved literature gives no structural placement of residue 45 within the WH1/EVH1 domain and no test of its binding to WIP or other partners; the only interaction modeling found concerns L101P.
payload.why_it_matters: Without knowing whether Thr45 sits at the WIP-binding interface or in the core fold, the mechanism cannot be assigned to a loss of binding versus a loss of folding.

payload.statement: No retrieved study tested Thr45Met for effects on actin polymerization or WASp-dependent signalling, so the downstream molecular consequence of this substitution is unestablished.
payload.why_it_matters: Only a functional readout would show whether the substitution impairs WASp activity or is functionally neutral at the cellular level, which is needed before calling it a loss-of-function mechanism.

Subject: variant_id=WAS-p.Thr45Met gene=WAS accession=P42768 position=45 reference=T alternate=M. Using evidence E1-E17 and gaps G1-G6 in the record, form competing agent-generated hypotheses for the mechanism of loss of function, say which the starting evidence favours, and state what would refute each.

payload.statement: The Thr45Met substitution sits in the WH1/EVH1 domain and removes a contact needed for WASp to bind its partner WIP, weakening the WASp–WIP complex and the downstream proline-rich-ligand recognition that depends on it.
payload.would_refute: If residue 45 is solvent-exposed and more than about 10 Å from the WIP-binding surface in PDB 9S9X and in a WASp–WIP model, and the Met substitution does not change the predicted WIP interface contacts or binding energy, the hypothesis is refuted.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Thr45 lies inside the EVH1 domain (E5, E6), an EVH1 domain binds proline-rich sequences (E16), and the only interaction modelling in the record shows a neighbouring EVH1 substitution disrupting a WIP contact (E15). The WASp–WIP complex structure (E10) is the one experimental structure that observes residue 45. Still missing: the actual location and contacts of residue 45 (G5), so the link is inferred from the domain and not shown for this residue.

payload.statement: The Thr45Met substitution destabilises the EVH1/WH1 fold, lowering folding stability and cellular WASp levels, so that little functional protein accumulates.
payload.would_refute: If residue 45 is buried in the high-confidence core of AF-P42768-F1 or 9S9X and a stability predictor gives a near-zero ΔΔG for T45M, and the Met side chain fits without clashes in the model, the destabilisation mechanism is refuted.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The strongest analogy is E15, where a neighbouring EVH1 substitution (L101P) severely suppresses WASp levels, which points to fold loss rather than only interface loss. The model is only moderately confident (mean pLDDT 69, E12), and the residue-level confidence is not in the record. The pathogenicity scores (E7–E9) fit either mechanism. No stability or expression data for T45M exists (G4), so this ranks below the interaction hypothesis.

payload.summary: Two competing agent-generated mechanisms for Thr45Met loss of function are recorded: H1 protein_interaction (WIP/proline-rich binding loss in the EVH1 domain, rank 1) and H2 stability_folding (EVH1 fold destabilisation with reduced WASp levels, rank 2). Each has a computational refutation test: residue-45 contact and interface change in 9S9X and a WASp–WIP model for H1, and core burial plus ΔΔG for H2. The main gaps are the residue-level location (G5), the absence of any functional or stability data for T45M (G1, G4), and the lack of a ligand in any structure (G3).

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change (ddG) for T45M on the AlphaFold model of P42768, via EBI ProtVar, with pLDDT at residue 45 and the other substitutions reported at that residue. Discriminates H2 (destabilisation) from H1 (interaction). A destabilising ddG at confident pLDDT supports H2; a neutral ddG at confident pLDDT refutes H2's stated criterion and shifts weight toward H1.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H2's own refutation criterion is a near-zero ddG with the side chain fitting in the model, so this test directly checks H2. A destabilising value would strengthen H2 over H1 and keep it favourite. A neutral value at high pLDDT would weaken H2 and leave H1 as the only remaining explanation, which would change the ranking. Limits: FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol, and the test says nothing about binding, so a neutral result does not confirm H1 on its own.

per_hypothesis.why: T2 found residue 45 in no predicted protein-protein interface (in_predicted_interface: false) and in none of the 1 P2Rank pockets (p2rank_pockets_containing_residue: []). Residue 45 does line 2 ProtVar pockets (pocket 5 score 572.2, buriedness 0.74; pocket 27 score 271.2, buriedness 0.79), which points away from a surface contact site. The would_refute criterion (solvent-exposed and more than about 10 Å from the WIP surface, with no change in interface contacts) was not met: T2 did not measure solvent exposure or distance to the WIP surface, and the interface call is marked not_covered. So the weakening is mild, not a refutation.

Residue 45 lies in two predicted pockets with high buriedness (0.74 and 0.79) on AF-P42768-F1, which is consistent with a buried, fold-relevant position. The pocket residues have mean pLDDT 84.0 and 85.4 (confidence control). This adds indirect support to H2 alongside T1 (FoldX ddG +3.56 kcal/mol, pLDDT 96.62 at residue 45). The would_refute criterion for H2 (buried residue with near-zero ddG and no clash) was not met, because T2 does not test the ddG and T1 gave +3.56 kcal/mol.

payload.uncertainty: T2 is a predicted-pocket and predicted-interface test on a single AlphaFold model (AF-P42768-F1, mean pLDDT 69.38 overall). Pocket membership and buriedness are computational predictions, not measured binding sites. The interface result is marked not_covered, so 'no interface' does not show that residue 45 is absent from the WIP interface. The buriedness values are pocket-level, not residue-level. The control results were: P2Rank 1 pocket, with no hit at residue 45; pocket confidence pLDDT 84.0 and 85.4. Neither T2 nor T1 used the WIP complex (9S9X) to measure distance to the WIP surface, so H1 cannot be refuted or confirmed from this test. Validation still needed: residue-level solvent accessibility and WIP-surface distance from 9S9X, and an experimental WASp level or folding measurement for T45M.

payload.description: Computational: on the WIP-complexed structure 9S9X (and AF-P42768-F1 as a control), compute residue-45 relative solvent accessibility (RSA) and the minimum heavy-atom distance from T45 to the WIP-binding surface. Apply the H1 would_refute criterion: refuted if T45 is solvent-exposed (RSA high) and more than about 10 Å from WIP. Supports H2 if T45 is buried (low RSA) and far from WIP, meaning H2 stands and H1 has no contact basis. Support H1 if T45 is within contact range of WIP. Outcome determines whether the H2 favoured call holds.
payload.why_now: T2 left H1 unrefuted but weakened, because its interface call was not_covered and it did not measure solvent exposure or distance to WIP. This is the test that H1's would_refute criterion actually requires. It is zero-compute, and it uses the experimental WIP complex (9S9X, observes residue 45) rather than predicted pockets.

payload.text:
## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of WAS p.Thr45Met (UniProt P42768), and which targeted computational tests check it? [E2] [G1]

## Evidence
Residue 45 lies in the WH1/EVH1 domain annotated by UniProt and InterPro [E5] [E6]. ClinVar lists the change as pathogenic with multiple submitters [E1], and UniProt records it as a natural variant in WAS-related disorder [E2]. gnomAD observed no occurrences of this allele [E3]. A literature report describes the change in an exon 2 X-linked thrombocytopenia family [E14]. No retrieved study measured WASp level, folding, or WIP binding for T45M [G4] [G5]. No functional assay covers residue 45 [G1], and no experimental structure carries the variant [G2].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1) proposes that T45M weakens WASp–WIP binding [H1]. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2) proposes that T45M destabilises the fold and lowers WASp levels [H2].

## Tests considered and the choice
Round 1: T1 (stability) was chosen. T2 (structural context) was rejected, as was T3 (structure comparison, which needed approval and 120 s) and T4 (ligand contact, which could not run) [T1] [T3] [T4].
Round 2, after H1 was reopened: T2 was chosen. T3 and T4 were rejected for the same reasons as before [T2].

## Result
T1 gave a FoldX ΔΔG of +3.56 kcal/mol for T45M on the AlphaFold model, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, at residue pLDDT 96.62 [T1] [E18]. The within-site control T45R gave +7.43 kcal/mol [E19]. T2 found residue 45 in two predicted pockets with buriedness 0.74 and 0.79 [E20] [E21], in no P2Rank pocket [E22], and in no predicted interface [T2].

## Updated decision
Round 1: H1 was favoured before T1 and H2 after, so the decision changed [D53]. Round 2: H2 was favoured before and after T2, so the decision did not change. T2 weakened H1 without refuting it [D74].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
All results are computational predictions on one AlphaFold model. The FoldX value is a prediction, not a measurement [T1]. Burial and solvent accessibility are not measured, and the pocket data are predicted [E20] [E21]. H1 is not refuted, because T2 did not measure distance to the WIP surface in 9S9X [E10] [D74]. Cellular WASp levels for T45M have not been measured [G4].

## Next experiment
Computational: compute residue-45 relative solvent accessibility and distance to the WIP surface on 9S9X and on the AlphaFold model, and run a second stability predictor (next experiment, seq 75 and seq 54) [E10] [D74]. A later wet-lab check would compare cellular WASp levels for T45M and wild type.
